Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited. To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes. This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books. Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration. Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses. In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06053515.

articles.title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking. We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome). From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80). Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

articles.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain. Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. 15 thoracic centres in the UK. Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023. Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision ollowed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision. The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications. 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12%  18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4%  12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12%  6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise. Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03677856.

articles.title: A Conversation Tool to Enhance Care for People With Type 2 Diabetes: The QBSafe Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Effective interventions are needed to support the cocreation of diabetes care plans that are sensible, desirable, and feasible for the people living with diabetes (ie, care that fits). To investigate whether an agenda-setting kit (ASK) added to usual primary care improves fit of care and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). This single-center, clinician-level cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from February 16, 2023, to July 26, 2024, with a 6-month follow-up, at a federally qualified health center in New Haven, Connecticut. Eligible clinicians were primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who prescribed medication to treat patients with T2D. Eligible patients were English- or Spanish-speaking adults aged 18 years or older with T2D and hemoglobin (Hb) A1c level greater than 8%. Patients were excluded if their clinician determined that an HbA1c level 8% or lower was inconsistent with goals of care. Data were analyzed from November 7, 2024, to August 13, 2026. Clinicians were randomized 1:1 to the ASK plus usual primary care group (intervention group) or usual primary care only (control group). The ASK intervention consisted of 14 conversation cards about life with diabetes and its treatment. Prior to the clinical encounter, patients were asked to select 0 to 3 cards they wanted to prioritize for discussion. The primary outcome was the 6-month change from baseline in illness intrusiveness measured with the Illness Intrusiveness Ratings Scale (IIRS; range: 13-91, with higher scores indicating greater intrusiveness) and HbA1c level. Secondary outcomes included changes in treatment burden measured with the Treatment Burden Questionnaire (TBQ; range: 0-150, with higher scores indicating greater burden), diabetes distress measured with the 17-Item Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS-17; scores: indicate little or no distress [<2.0], moderate distress [2.0-2.9], and high distress [≥3.0]), and visit satisfaction. Eleven clinicians (6 [54.5%] female) were included in the trial along with 143 of their patients. The mean (SD) patient age was 56 (12) years; 87 participants (60.8%) were female and 88 (61.5%) reported Spanish as their primary language. Six-month survey data were available for 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) in the intervention group and 58 of 69 (84.0%) in the control group; data on HbA1c level were available for 71 (95.9%) and 65 (94.2%), respectively. At 6 months, mean (SD) IIRS scores were 32.1 (15.1) and 37.1 (18.7) in the intervention and control groups (adjusted mean difference, -3.9; 95% CI, -10.4 to 2.6). The mean (SD) HbA1c levels were 8.8% (1.8) in the intervention group and 9.1% (1.8) in the control group (adjusted mean difference, -0.2%; 95% CI, -0.9% to 0.5%). Mean (SD) TBQ scores in the intervention and control groups were 41.2 (44.8) and 46.8 (44.4) (adjusted mean difference, 1.0; 95% CI, -16.6 to 18.6), and mean (SD) DDS-17 scores were 2.0 (1.0) and 2.3 (1.0) (adjusted mean difference, -0.1; 95% CI, -0.4 to 0.2). Clinician-reported satisfaction was greater in the intervention group; patient satisfaction did not differ between groups. In this cluster randomized clinical trial of adults with T2D, use of the ASK with usual primary care was associated with greater clinician satisfaction but not with improvements in patients' fit of care or glycemic control over 6 months. Larger studies should evaluate interventions that not only identify patients' priorities and treatment burdens but also better support clinicians in addressing them. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05553912.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.
articles.abstract: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear. In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32). Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

articles.title: Selective Reduction in Monochorionic Pregnancies With Selective Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Published studies of selective reduction in monochorionic pregnancies often include multiple indications, limiting outcome estimates specific to selective fetal growth restriction. To estimate the rates of co-twin intrauterine fetal demise, co-twin neonatal demise, and gestational age at delivery in monochorionic pregnancies complicated by selective fetal growth restriction undergoing selective reduction and stratify the outcomes according to the surgical technique. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through May 2026. Studies were eligible if they reported monochorionic pregnancies complicated by selective fetal growth restriction undergoing selective reduction with data on co-twin intrauterine fetal demise or neonatal demise and gestational age at delivery. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and registered with the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (INPLASY202580001). Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis, and technique differences were evaluated using meta-analytic tests for subgroup differences. Post hoc binomial generalized linear mixed models assessed the robustness of dichotomous outcomes without continuity correction. I² quantified heterogeneity across studies. Studies were eligible if they reported monochorionic pregnancies complicated by selective fetal growth restriction undergoing selective reduction with data on co-twin intrauterine fetal demise or neonatal demise and gestational age at delivery. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and registered with the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (INPLASY;INPLASY202580001). Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis, and technique differences were evaluated using meta-analytic tests for subgroup differences. Post hoc binomial generalized linear mixed models assessed the robustness of dichotomous outcomes without continuity correction. I quantified heterogeneity across studies. A total of 22 studies, including 686 pregnancies, met the inclusion criteria and were eligible for quantitative synthesis. The overall rates of co-twin intrauterine fetal demise and co-twin neonatal death were 15% and 4%, respectively, and the gestational age at delivery was 35.4 weeks (95% confidence interval, 34.2-36.6). In the primary indirect study-level subgroup analysis, pooled co-twin intrauterine fetal demise was higher in radiofrequency ablation than bipolar cord coagulation studies (20% vs 9%; P=.02). In the generalized linear mixed model sensitivity analysis, the estimated rates remained higher in radiofrequency ablation than bipolar cord coagulation studies (14.8% vs 6.6%), but the subgroup difference was not statistically significant (P=.06). The only direct within-study comparison included 24 selective fetal growth restriction pregnancies and showed no significant difference in co-twin intrauterine fetal demise (bipolar cord coagulation, 0/5; radiofrequency ablation, 3/19; P=1.00). Co-twin neonatal death rates were comparable (bipolar cord coagulation, 5% vs radiofrequency ablation, 3%). Gestational age at delivery was lower in cases undergoing bipolar cord coagulation compared with radiofrequency ablation (34.5 weeks vs 36.8 weeks, respectively; P=.039). These unadjusted comparisons may be confounded by differences in study and case characteristics. In monochorionic pregnancies complicated by selective fetal growth restriction undergoing selective reduction, pooled risks of co-twin intrauterine fetal demise and neonatal death were approximately 15% and 4%, respectively. The primary analysis suggested lower co-twin intrauterine fetal demise and earlier delivery in bipolar cord coagulation than radiofrequency ablation studies; however, the statistical evidence for the intrauterine fetal demise difference was weaker in the generalized linear mixed model sensitivity analysis, and all technique comparisons were indirect, unadjusted, potentially confounded, and the single direct comparison was small and inconclusive. Available evidence does not establish an advantage of bipolar cord coagulation or radiofrequency ablation.

articles.abstract: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete. Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). articles.title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications. The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications. A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%). A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

articles.title: Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency is present in >50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and is associated with reduced exercise capacity and survival. Whether iron repletion improves exercise capacity as objectively measured by peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]) is unknown. The IRONMET-HFpEF trial (Impact of Intravenous Iron Repletion on Mechanisms of Exercise Intolerance in HFpEF) sought to determine whether ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared with placebo improves peak [Formula: see text] in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency. This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency, defined as ferritin <100 ng/mL or <300 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%. Participants were enrolled between December 2021 and April 2026. Single-dose ferric derisomaltose (1000 mg; n=44) or placebo (n=21) was administered once intravenously. The primary end point was the change in peak [Formula: see text] from baseline to 12 weeks with an analysis of covariance model including terms for treatment group, baseline peak [Formula: see text], and sex. Secondary end points included changes in [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, New York Heart Association class, health status assessed by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score, and iron biomarkers at 12 weeks. Among 65 randomized participants (median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 58-76 years], 72% women, transferrin saturation 16.0±7.4%, ferritin 57.8±48.9 ng/mL), 64 (98.5%) completed the study. The median baseline peak [Formula: see text] was 12.7 mL·kg·min (interquartile range, 10.6-15.8 mL·kg·min) in the FDI group and 12.2 mL·kg·min (11.6-14.6 mL·kg·min) in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, peak [Formula: see text] improved by 1.2 mL·kg·min (95% CI, 0.6-1.7) in the FDI group and was unchanged (0.1 mL·kg·min [95% CI, -0.7 to 0.9]) in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, 1.1 mL·kg·min [95% CI, 0.2-1.9]; =0.02). [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, and New York Heart Association class also improved in the FDI compared with the placebo group (all <0.05), whereas the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score did not differ significantly between groups (FDI group, +4.4 [95% CI, -2.4 to 11.2]; =0.20). FDI increased transferrin saturation (9.4% [95% CI, 4.9%-13.9%]) and ferritin (183 ng/mL [95% CI, 128-238]) compared with the placebo group (<0.001 for both). There were no serious adverse events related to FDI administration. In the largest trial to date of iron repletion in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency, FDI improved multiple measures of exercise capacity. articles.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
articles.abstract: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies. In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; =0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Although numerous treatment approaches are recommended by international clinical guidelines, there is still limited understanding of which interventions provide the best value for money. We aimed to critically appraise and summarise the evidence on the cost-effectiveness and costs of interventions endorsed in recent guidelines to manage low back pain (LBP), compared to usual care. We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. The primary outcome was cost/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), which was converted to 2024 Great British Pound values, tabulated and summarised qualitatively. Secondary outcomes were direct costs (total, interventional, health service use, community services and out-of-pocket costs) and indirect costs (e.g., lost wages, lost productivity, absenteeism). We assessed methodological quality using the Consensus Health Economics Criteria (CHEC) checklist for within-trial economic evaluations or the Philips checklist for modelling studies. Our review included 20 studies (17 within-trial economic evaluations and three modelling studies), published between 2005 and 2026. Half (n = 10) focussed on chronic LBP (>3-month duration), and eight included mixed populations (i.e., acute, subacute and chronic). All studies were of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, both single-modality and multimodal interventions (e.g., exercise plus spinal manipulation; diet plus physical activity). Most interventions are cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000. Moreover, interventions aiming to reduce fear and stress or support self-management in people with chronic LBP, as well as clinician-delivered interventions including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support are potentially cost-saving from the healthcare, societal and payer's perspectives, as they are both more effective and less costly than usual care (e.g., first contact management, including advice and medication). All of the evidence is derived from high-income countries, and from a considerable heterogenous body of literature. Evidence on cost-effective treatments in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions that include education, psychological support, acupuncture and exercise seem to be cost-effective for managing LBP, compared to usual care. Improved access to and implementation of these effective treatments is urgently needed so more people can benefit from them in routine care. The review was registered on PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk; CRD42024510270).

structuredAbstract.text: We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. articles.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. articles.title: Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
articles.abstract: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo. A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects. Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%). Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glucose values versus venous plasma glucose values during oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) in youths with obesity, their effect on glycemic classification, and whether deconvolution-based reconstruction improves agreement. Twenty-nine youths with obesity underwent OGTT while wearing a FreeStyle Libre 2 sensor. Raw CGM values were temporally aligned with venous plasma glucose values and used to reconstruct plasma profiles via a first-order plasma-interstitial kinetic model and inverse filtering. Accuracy, agreement, consensus error grid, and glycemic classification were compared with collected venous plasma glucose values. Temporally aligned CGM-derived values showed limited agreement with collected venous plasma glucose values (mean absolute relative difference [MARD] 12.96%; 51.72% of values within ±10 mg/dL; 20.06% of values differing by >25 mg/dL) and caused classification shifts. After reconstruction, MARD decreased to 5.55%, the proportion of values within ±10 mg/dL increased to 75.86%, almost all values fell within consensus error grid zone A, and classification shifts were reduced. Deconvolution-based CGM reconstruction may support plasma-referenced, less invasive OGTT-based dysglycemic assessment.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of RCTs Using Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is a reasonable alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC versus OAC in patients with AF. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/all-cause death. The primary safety endpoint was major bleeding. Secondary endpoints included net adverse clinical events, all-cause death, nonprocedure-related bleeding, and ischemic stroke. Reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis using a 2-stage approach and study-level meta-analysis using random-effects models were performed. Six trials enrolling 7,004 patients randomized to LAAC (n = 3,681) or OAC (n = 3,323) were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC versus OAC for the primary efficacy endpoint (difference in restricted mean survival time [∆RMST] -0.006 years, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.027 to 0.015 years, p = 0.56) or primary safety endpoint (∆RMST 0.004 years, 95% CI -0.025 to 0.034 years, p = 0.77) at 3 years. Nonprocedure-related bleeding was significantly lower with LAAC versus OAC (∆RMST 0.162 years, 95% CI 0.104 to 0.220 years, p <0.001) with no difference in all-cause death (∆RMST 0.029 years, 95% CI -0.031 to 0.089 years, p = 0.34). In a study-level meta-analysis, ischemic stroke was not significantly different with LAAC versus OAC (risk ratio 1.32, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.86, p = 0.09). In conclusion, the trade-off between a statistically significant lower risk of nonprocedure-related bleeding and a numerically, but not statistically, higher risk of ischemic stroke with LAAC versus OAC necessitates individualized risk assessment and shared decision-making for patients with AF at elevated risk of stroke.

articles.title: Interventions to Support Parents Whose Babies Cry Excessively: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Parents report that around 10% to 20% of babies cry a lot without an apparent reason during early infancy. This "excessive" infant crying can lead to adverse outcomes, including parental depression, breastfeeding cessation, impaired parent-child relationships, and, in extreme cases, infant abuse. Cost-effective parent-support services are needed. To assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of interventions designed to support parents of excessively crying babies. MEDLINE, Embase, EconLit, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, CINAHL and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 8th April 2025. The NIHR CRN database and handsearching were used to identify further studies. Comparative studies reporting parental outcomes for any intervention supporting parents of excessively crying infants aged ≤1 year were included. Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed when possible; otherwise, narrative synthesis was conducted. Meta-analysis found that educational interventions significantly reduced parental stress or anxiety. Narrative analyses produced mixed findings, but components common to successful educational interventions were indicated. Meta-analyses of studies administering probiotics to infants found significant improvements in parents' quality of life but not in parental depression. No safety data and limited economic evidence were found. Few studies measured similar enough parental outcomes to be pooled in meta-analysis. Risk of bias ranged from unclear to high risk. Educational and probiotic interventions show promise for supporting parents of excessively crying babies. Additional controlled trials employing evidence-based interventions and outcome measures and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to build on these findings.

articles.title: International recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica.
articles.abstract: The study aims to develop international recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). An international, multidisciplinary task force of 30 members from 12 countries was convened; the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standard operating procedures were followed. Six clinical key questions addressing the role of imaging (ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) in diagnosis, monitoring, outcome prediction, and technical aspects in PMR were the basis for a systematic literature review. Recommendations were formulated based on evidence and expert opinion and refined iteratively until consensus was achieved. The level of agreement was assessed by voting. Three overarching principles and 7 recommendations were developed. PMR remains primarily a clinical diagnosis. Imaging is neither required to confirm PMR in patients with a high clinical probability of the disease nor to exclude PMR in case of low clinical probability. Imaging is most useful in patients with intermediate pretest probability (ie, atypical presentations or suspected alternative/overlapping conditions). No single imaging modality demonstrated sufficient accuracy to be recommended as a first-line test; therefore, imaging should be individualised according to clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, access, and local expertise. Vascular imaging should be performed when overlap with giant cell arteritis is suspected, whereas systematic screening for subclinical vasculitis is not supported by current evidence. Utilising imaging for disease monitoring or outcome prediction is currently not recommended. These recommendations provide the first evidence-based guidance for the use of imaging in PMR, reinforcing clinical assessment as the cornerstone of diagnosis and positioning imaging as a context-driven adjunct.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To compare the effects of aerobic exercise, resistance exercise, and combined interventions on pain, function, and quality of life (QoL) in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA) at the short term (≤12 weeks) and long term (>12 weeks).  Intervention systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA).  MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL, PEDro, AMED, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception until July 2025.  We included randomized controlled trials of patients with knee OA that evaluated exercise interventions aimed at improving pain, function, and QoL.  Using random-effects models, the NMA synthesized effect sizes and ranked interventions by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), with evidence certainty assessed via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.  Thirty-five trials (n = 3808 patients) were included. For pain, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect among the interventions (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.937, low certainty). For function, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect estimates (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), followed by long-term aerobic exercise (SMD = -0.540, very low certainty). Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) for improving QoL.  Aerobic and resistance exercise, alone or in combination, and delivered over the short- or long-term, improved pain, function, and QoL for patients with knee OA. Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had clinically meaningful improvements for pain, with relatively favorable effects on function and QoL. Evidence regarding the clinical significance of long-term exercise interventions was limited. .

articles.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; =0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47];  < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. articles.title: Home Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Gamified Cognitive Control Training for Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. articles.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I=62·9%; τ=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I=99·2%; τ=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I=97·8%; τ=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. articles.title: Near-infrared Autofluorescence Probe Versus Visual Identification for Parathyroid Detection and Functional Preservation During Total Thyroidectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: To assess whether PTeye-guided identification increases the number of parathyroid glands (PGs) preserved in situ and reduces hypoparathyroidism compared with visual identification alone. Injury or inadvertent removal of PGs during thyroidectomy is the main cause of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. Reliance on visual inspection makes intraoperative PG identification difficult. Probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) systems such as PTeye provide real-time, tissue-specific feedback that may enhance PG detection and preservation. In this single-center, prospective, randomized trial, patients undergoing first-time total thyroidectomy were allocated to PTeye-assisted or visual PG identification. Procedures were performed by 2 senior and 3 junior surgeons. The primary outcome was the number of PGs identified. Secondary outcomes included inadvertent parathyroidectomy, autotransplantation, and transient and last follow-up hypoparathyroidism. Among 154 randomized patients (77 per group; mean age 53.4±14.3 y; 84.4% female), PTeye increased the mean number of PGs identified (3.81 vs. 2.73; P <0.001) and the proportion with 3-4 PGs preserved in situ (98.7% vs. 87.0%; P =0.004). Inadvertent parathyroidectomy was less frequent with PTeye (5.2% vs. 20.8%; P =0.004). Junior surgeons performed more autotransplantations than senior surgeons when using PTeye (33.3% vs. 10.5%; P =0.015). Female sex ( P =0.047), ≤2 PGs preserved ( P =0.008), and autotransplantation ( P =0.010) predicted low postoperative day-1 parathormone serum level. Among junior surgeons, transient hypoparathyroidism was lower with PTeye (20.5% vs. 55.2%; P <0.001), with no difference among senior surgeons. Permanent hypoparathyroidism rates were similar between groups. PTeye-guided NIRAF improves PG identification and in situ preservation and reduces transient hypoparathyroidism, particularly for junior surgeons, without affecting permanent hypoparathyroidism.

articles.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjogren's Disease.
articles.abstract: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor. We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48. Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups. In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

articles.title: Imaging for diagnosis, monitoring and outcome prediction in polymyalgia rheumatica: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis informing an international task force.
articles.abstract: To summarise evidence on imaging for the diagnosis, monitoring and outcome prediction in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) to inform an international task force. Six research questions across diagnostic, monitoring, prognostic and technical aspects were defined. A systematic literature review searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, Epistemonikos and the Cochrane Library (through July 2025), including prospective and retrospective cohort studies (≥20 patients) as well as case–control and cross-sectional studies for diagnostic aspects. Test performance was summarised descriptively and meta-analysed using bivariate random-effects models when ≥2 low or some concerns on risk-of-bias (RoB) studies were available. Forty-nine studies were included: 32 on diagnosis, 6 on monitoring, 13 on outcome prediction and 8 on technical aspects (some studies covered ≥1 aspect). No study was graded as low RoB. Diagnostic studies identified useful imaging lesions (eg, extracapsular and bilateral inflammatory patterns of shoulders and hips), but few were validated in independent cohorts. Diagnostic accuracy of positron emission tomography scores was reduced in the case of prior treatment and when used to differentiate PMR from other inflammatory diseases. Glucocorticoids substantially reduced sensitivity across modalities, highlighting the value of timely imaging when indicated. Data on monitoring and outcome prediction were sparse and heterogeneous. This systematic literature review serves as a basis for the formulation of international recommendations on the use of imaging in PMR. Available evidence was heterogeneous and of limited quality but revealed distinct imaging lesions and scores that can support PMR diagnosis. Well-designed prospective studies and external validations are needed.

articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively. Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity. Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes and Recovery After Robot-Assisted vs Open Radical Hysterectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the RACC Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy was introduced to reduce perioperative morbidity in early-stage cervical cancer, but concerns regarding oncologic safety have limited its use. High-quality prospective randomized data evaluating perioperative safety and recovery after robot-assisted radical hysterectomy remain limited. To compare perioperative safety and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) after robot-assisted vs open radical hysterectomy. The Robot-Assisted Approach to Cervical Cancer (RACC) trial, a multicenter, noninferiority, phase 3 randomized clinical trial, was conducted at tertiary centers in Europe. Female participants aged 18 years and older with cervical cancer (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics [FIGO] 2018 stage IB [excluding IB3] or IIA1) were enrolled. Patients were randomized between 2019 and 2025. Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy. Prespecified secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications (graded using standardized classification systems), postoperative complications within 30 days (Clavien-Dindo), and HRQOL at 1 month (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Cervical Cancer Module, and EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level questionnaire). These prespecified secondary analyses were exploratory and were not powered for confirmatory inference. Of 900 randomized patients (robotic surgery, median [IQR] age, 46 [39-53] years; open surgery, median [IQR] age, 45 [37-54] years), 809 (90%) were included in the intraoperative safety analysis, 798 (89%) in the postoperative safety analysis, and 723 (80%) in the 1-month HRQOL analysis. Intraoperative complications occurred in 24 of 419 patients (5.7%) in the robot-assisted group vs 39 of 390 patients (10.0%) in the open surgery group (risk difference, -4.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.0 to -0.6 percentage points); most were minor, whereas major complications were infrequent and similar. Postoperative complications within 30 days were similar (33.4% vs 34.8%; risk difference, -1.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.9 to 5.2 percentage points), including readmission and reoperation. At 1 month, robot-assisted surgery was associated with small differences in selected domains, including physical functioning (+5 points; 95% CI, 3-8 points), role functioning (+8 points; 95% CI, 4-13 points), and lower pain (+5 points; 95% CI, 2-9 points), whereas most domains did not meet thresholds for clinically important differences. Results of this secondary analysis of the RACC randomized clinical trial show that robot-assisted radical hysterectomy was associated with fewer intraoperative complications, primarily reflecting lower-grade events, with similar postoperative morbidity compared with open surgery. Differences in early HRQOL were small, and overall findings indicate no improvement in clinically consequential postoperative outcomes or recovery. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03719547.

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety. A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively. articles.title: Acupuncture for older adults with dementia in residential care homes: an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Dementia harms the mental health of older adults and poses a significant caregiver burden. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture in managing cognitive decline and related symptoms in older adults with dementia. Eligible participants were recruited from 19 local residential care homes for older people in Hong Kong, China, from 5 October 2021 to 27 August 2024, in an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial. 118 participants were randomised to acupuncture and care-as-usual control (n=59 in each group) for 12 weeks. The analyses were on the intention-to-treat population. The primary outcome was the mean baseline-to-endpoint change of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included the functional independence, pain, depressive and sleep symptoms. 85.6% (101/118) of participants completed the study. The primary outcome, MoCA, was not significantly improved in week 12. Subgroup analyses showed that the treatment effect on MoCA appeared to differ across dementia severity strata. Acupuncture was superior over control in improving functional independence (the Chinese version of the Modified Barthel Index, mean difference=4.12, 95% confidence interval=0.81, 7.44, P=0.015; standardised effect size=0.29). All treatment-related adverse events were mild, and 2 nontreatment-related death cases were reported. While no significant effect in cognitive function was observed, acupuncture was associated with an improvement in functional independence, and the treatment effect on cognition might differ across dementia severity strata. This warrants further validation of the exploratory results, identifying a subpopulation of older adults with dementia who could gain more benefits from acupuncture in improving cognitive function. www.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04305951, date of registration: 10/03/2020.

articles.title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

articles.title: The Smart MDI System in People With Type 1 Diabetes and High HBA1C: A Randomized Controlled Trial Demonstrating That Response to Alerts Drives Outcomes.
articles.abstract: The aim was to assess the efficacy and safety of the smart multiple daily injections (MDI) system versus MDI plus continuous glucose monitor (CGM) in people with Type 1 diabetes and HbA1c ≥ 8%. After a 3-week run-in, 143 participants were randomized to Smart MDI or MDI + CGM. The primary endpoint was between-group difference (Δ) in time-in-range (TIR) at 6 months, adjusted for baseline glycaemia and assessed for non-inferiority (margin 7.5%). Secondary endpoints included HbA1c (non-inferiority margin 0.4%) and superiority analyses for TIR and HbA1c. Smart MDI alerts prompt insulin bolus actions (in contrast to traditional CGM alerts), and post hoc analyses were performed to evaluate 'alert-responsiveness' on glycaemia. Alert-responsiveness findings were validated in a real-world cohort of 5507 users. Safety endpoints were assessed. At 6 months, Δ TIR between groups was 0.19 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -4.9 to 5.3), thus meeting non-inferiority; HbA1c also met non-inferiority (Δ: -0.13 percentage points, -0.46 to 0.19) but neither showed superiority. Post hoc analyses showed higher responders to alerts (those responding more than the median response rate of 28.3%, n = 31) had greater TIR gains than lower responders (n = 28) (+8.12 percentage points; p = 0.04) and HbA1c reduction (-0.6 percentage points; p = 0.02). TIR benefits in higher responders were confirmed in the real-world cohort. One episode of diabetic ketoacidosis occurred (run-in) and one severe hypoglycaemic event occurred (control arm). Smart MDI is safe and non-inferior, achieving non-inferiority to MDI + CGM regarding TIR and HbA1c. Responding to as few as 28% of alerts resulted in glycaemic improvements.

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. articles.title: Curcumin Suppresses Growth of Recurrent Colorectal Adenoma After Endoscopic Resection: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial.
articles.abstract: Experimental and limited clinical studies suggest that curcumin has chemopreventive activity in the colorectum. This large-scale clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of curcumin in patients with previously endoscopically resected colorectal neoplasia. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial enrolled patients with previously resected colorectal neoplasia. Eligible patients were randomly assigned (1:1), using a stratified, computer-generated scheme to receive oral submicron-powdered curcumin (Theracurmin; 180 mg twice daily) or identical placebo capsules for 2 years. All analyses were performed according to a modified intention-to-treat principle including all randomly assigned patients who underwent the 2-year colonoscopy. Between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2020, 577 patients were randomly assigned to curcumin (n = 287) or placebo groups (n = 290). The detection rate of recurrent colorectal adenomas at 2 years, the primary end point, did not differ significantly between groups (risk ratio 0.98; 95% confident interval 0.82-1.16). However, the detection rate of adenomas ≥6 mm, a prespecified lesion category recommended for endoscopic resection in Japanese guidelines, was significantly lower with curcumin (risk ratio, 0.56; 95% confident interval, 0.33-0.95; P = 0.04). The per-patient number of adenomas ≥6 mm was also significantly lower ( P = 0.03), and the median size of all detected adenomas was significantly smaller in the curcumin group ( P = 0.003). The inhibitory effect seemed more pronounced in patients with higher baseline adenoma burden and in men in exploratory analyses. Treatment-related adverse events were infrequent and mild. Curcumin inhibited the growth of recurrent colorectal adenomas, despite no significant reduction in the overall incidence of recurrence. This is the first large-scale randomized clinical trial demonstrating the suppressive efficacy of curcumin against colorectal neoplasia, and also highlighting the importance of incorporating growth-related endpoints, in addition to incidence-based or detection-based end points, in chemoprevention studies (jRCTs061180079).

articles.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting. Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns. Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis. Novartis.
